turnaround_reason: Inspire, a former high-flyer in implantable obstructive-sleep-apnea therapy, fell from ~$147 to a $38.91 low (now ~$62) on GLP-1-driven TAM fears and a 2026 guidance cut tied to coding/reimbursement problems for its new Inspire V system and the WISeR prior-authorization program. It is basing while the reimbursement picture resolves.
bullish_points: Exceptional business quality: 86% gross margins, net cash balance sheet ($321M cash vs $29M debt), and a differentiated implantable therapy with a wide moat
Q2 2026 delivered a profit and a guidance raise that popped the stock ~20% — early sign the reimbursement air-pocket may be transient
Multi-year secular demand for OSA treatment is intact; GLP-1s address a different patient segment and adherence remains poor
Inspire V is a genuine product-cycle upgrade once coding/reimbursement normalizes
bearish_points: Management cut full-year 2026 guidance on Inspire V coding and WISeR reimbursement uncertainty; revenue is still guided down 4-10% YoY
Reimbursement risk for a discretionary implant is the exact kind of overhang that can persist for several quarters
GLP-1 narrative, even if overstated, keeps a valuation lid on the multiple
Mixed signals — an earlier guidance slash then a Q2 beat — make the trajectory hard to underwrite
catalyst: Resolution of Inspire V coding/reimbursement and WISeR clarity, plus continued quarterly proof the revenue decline is bottoming
catalyst_timing: Q3-Q4 2026 earnings and CMS/payer coding updates
suggested_trade: Small starter spot near $60 on the quality; scale up only once reimbursement clarity and revenue re-acceleration are confirmed.
key_risk: Reimbursement/coding problems drag on and revenue keeps declining, proving the guidance cut was structural not transient
would_skip_if: You need reimbursement resolution in hand before paying up for the quality
